author: Nick Visser
description:
Players can renovate houses, fix cars, lift weights and follow the story in Grand Theft Auto VI’s Miami-inspired Vice City

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

Gamers across Australia woke up Thursday morning feeling like Christmas had come early, some bleary-eyed from late-night sessions on the PlayStation, others with grand plans for a weekend foray in Vice City when their day jobs let them loose.

Grand Theft Auto VI, more than a decade in the making, is here. And the reviews, mere hours into release, reflect universal acclaim. The game has already vaulted to the top spot on Metacritic’s list of the best games of all time, sitting above 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with an unprecedented 99/100 score.
title: GTA 6 dazzles gamers in Australia with ‘fully lived-in, breathable world’

author: Associated Press
description:
The autonomous driving company suspended driverless taxi rides on US highways days after California banned the vehicles on its own freeways

Waymo has stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways across the US indefinitely. The Alphabet subsidiary pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after California banned them from freeways in response to recent traffic incidents.

Waymo had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas, including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver. Those rides remain unaffected by suspended freeway service.

Continue reading...
title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from freeways across the US after California ban

author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
description:
High court judge issues order against Raise the Colours over flags on council-owned street furniture

The campaign group Raise the Colours has been temporarily banned from placing union jacks on lamp-posts and roundabouts in Birmingham after a legal challenge by the local council.

The high court judge Emma Kelly granted an interim injunction banning the placing of all flags on council-owned street furniture without prior permission in a judgment issued on Wednesday, Birmingham city council said.

Continue reading...
title: Birmingham council granted interim ban on union jacks on lamp-posts

author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
description:
Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago

Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.

Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

Continue reading...
title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military

author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
description:
Home secretary says ‘routine two-tier policing’ does not exist, but public trust in impartial law enforcement must be restored

Shabana Mahmood has backed a ban on police officers marching in pride events in uniform as she said there had been a “few examples” of two-tier policing.

Although she said there was no systematic or routine two-tier policing, the home secretary said “a new impartiality standard” was necessary to reverse the fall in the public’s faith in law enforcement.

Continue reading...
title: Shabana Mahmood backs ban on police marching in pride events in uniform

author: Timothy Pratt
description:
DoJ cites three examples of alterations from English into Spanish for James ‘Fergie’ Chambers after Guardian report

US authorities have admitted altering the translation of an extradition request for James “Fergie” Chambers from English into Spanish, attributing violent and illegal actions to the wealthy activist and philanthropist that were not in the original.

Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

Continue reading...
title: US admits ‘substantial’ change to extradition request translation for leftist activist

author: Lois Beckett
description:
Flood advisories issued for much of Bay Area with coastal flooding and heavy surf possible in southern California

Heavy rain or snowfall is predicted across California this week, as an “atmospheric river” dumps precipitation across the state.

Flood advisories have been issued for much of the Bay Area, according to the National Weather Service (NWS), while southern California may see coastal flooding, heavy surf, wave damage to coastal piers and parking lots, and beach sand erosion.

Continue reading...
title: Heavy rain and snow predicted in California as ‘atmospheric river’ moves across state

author: Ariana Baio
description:
The comments come as the top US transportation official faces scrutiny over his handling of the tech outage crisis

The head of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) took responsibility for the nationwide ground stop that affected more than 12,400 flights on Friday, urging people to “lay off” Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary.

“I take full responsibility for it,” Bryan Bedford, the FAA administrator, said at an event featuring aviation officials and lawmakers on Wednesday, Politico reported.
title: FAA administrator urges ‘lay off’ Sean Duffy for the flight stoppage: ‘Blame me’

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Committee chair Bill Cassidy, a Republican, said Jim O’Neill ‘did not do enough to stand up for science’ in previous posts

Jim O’Neill will not undergo a confirmation hearing on Wednesday to head he National Science Foundation (NSF) because he “did not do enough to stand up for science” in his previous position, said Bill Cassidy, a Republican from Louisiana who is chair of the Senate committee on health, education, labor and pensions.

This ends O’Neill’s run for the top US scientific organization, an embattled independent federal agency that has seen major budget cuts and grant freezes under the Trump administration. The next NSF nominee will face a Democratic-led Senate.

Continue reading...
title: Senate committee rejects Trump nominee to lead National Science Foundation

author: Maya Yang
description:
Andrew M Kozak, 41, pleaded not guilty to two charges in federal court after an explosive device was found at facility

A 41-year-old man has been charged in connection to last week’s bomb threat at an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois.

On Tuesday, the justice department charged Andrew M Kozak, 41, of Chillicothe, Illinois, with one count of transmitting a threat through interstate or foreign commerce to unlawfully damage or destroy the plant using fire and an explosive, as well as one count of making threatening interstate communications.

Continue reading...
title: Man charged in connection to bomb threat at Illinois ethanol plant

author: Ariana Baio in New York
description:
As Democrats flag AI bank breaches and cyber-attacks in Japan, Jay Clayton says system failures happen

  • US politics live – latest updates

A bipartisan pair of US senators are calling on Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence and AI czar, to identify and fix vulnerabilities in the US’s infrastructure following nationwide outages at major companies and government agencies.

Maria Cantwell, the top Democrat on the Senate commerce, science, and transportation committee, and Mike Rounds, the Republican chair of the Senate subcommittee on cyb
title: US senators urge White House AI chief to fix vulnerabilities after mass outages

author: Sam Levin
description:
California Democrats flipped five seats and will send 48 representatives to DC after successful redistricting effort

California Republicans have taken an extraordinary hit in the midterm elections, with only four of the state’s 52 congressional seats going to GOP representatives, leaving the party with its smallest delegation to Washington in decades.

California Democrats flipped five seats and will be sending 48 representatives to Washington DC for the new term. The result stems from the successful redistricting effort spearheaded by the state’s Democratic governor, Gavin Newsom, as well as a seismic blue wave has knocked out R
title: California Republicans won only four of state’s 52 US House seats in midterms

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Dengane Omari Jack filed a lawsuit against his landlord and multiple construction companies

A Brooklyn man who lost his home in the building collapse that killed eight people last week has said he raised concerns about visible cracks in the brickwork weeks before the disaster.

Dengane Omari Jack, 48, made the allegations in a lawsuit filed against his landlord and multiple construction companies after the apartment building on Flatbush Avenue collapsed into a neighboring construction site on 11 November.

Continue reading...
title: Brooklyn man sues, saying he warned of cracks before deadly building collapse

author: Johana Bhuiyan
description:
Exclusive: three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms

A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

On Wednesday, senators Ron Wyden, Ed Markey and Ben Luján sent letters to the CEOs of the tech companies, saying the safeguards they have in place to keep nudification off their app stores or platforms are not sufficient.

Continue reading...
title: Senators criticize Apple and Google for letting teens access ‘nudify’ apps despite parental controls

author: Tom McIlroy in Shenzhen
description:
Despite pleas from pro-Ukraine Australians, the prime minister accepts wishes of Chinese hosts with group picture

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese has appeared in a leaders’ photo with Vladimir Putin at the Apec summit in China, despite Australia’s Ukrainian community urging the prime minister to protest against Russia’s war.

After arriving in the Chinese tech capital, Shenzhen, on Wednesday, Albanese said he would respect the wishes of China as the hosts of this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit and take part in the photo.

Continue reading...</
title: Anthony Albanese defies critics for Apec summit photo with Vladimir Putin

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Landfill operators have been ordered to provide hotel accommodations and other care to area residents

Officials in a Los Angeles county have ordered the operators of a landfill to provide hotel accommodations and other care to nearby residents after it exploded with decomposing garbage and methane gas.

A noxious, dark geyser of material and smoke began to spew from the troubled Chiquita Canyon landfill on Monday afternoon, prompting officials to issue advisories for nearby communities.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Plume’ of decomposing garbage and gas prompts emergency health order for LA county residents

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Research by InfluenceMap raises questions about association’s policies and representation, particularly around advocacy for new gas supplies

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Business Council of Australia is lobbying for gas expansion policies that clash with the climate concerns of the majority of its own members, according to new research that raises questions about the sway of a handful of major companies.

The business association also does not publicly disclose who is on its energy and climate committee, prompting transparency concerns among researchers over how its policies are shaped and whose interests they represent.
title: Business Council of Australia more aligned with fossil fuel industry than its members’ values, analysis finds

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Archibald Amory, 58, reportedly being held in Tennessee pending return to New York, where he was tied to two cases

A man has been arrested in Nashville after DNA linked him to a series of unsolved New York City rapes from the 1990s, according to a news report.

Archibald Amory, 58, was detained on Thursday in Hermitage, a neighborhood of Nashville, and is being held there pending his return to New York City, according to the Daily News, citing sources and Nashville authorities.

Continue reading...
title: Man arrested in Nashville after DNA links him to unsolved 1990s rape cases

author: Hilary Beaumont
description:
GOP lawmakers are rushing through high-priority bills before newly elected Democrats are sworn in

Climate groups fear lawmakers could pass a bill by the end of the year that would give fossil fuel companies immunity from lawsuits and legislation that aims to hold them accountable for the climate crisis.

After the blue wave election, Republican lawmakers are rushing to pass high-priority bills before newly elected Democrats are sworn in. Hundreds of elected leaders and climate groups sent a letter to Democratic leadership urging them to reject any proposal that would shield fossil fuel companies from liability for the climate crisis.

Continue reading...
title: Republicans could expedite bill to make big oil immune to lawsuits, warn experts

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Senate Democratic leader hails result which will give the party a commanding 56-44 seat majority

  • Trump in China for Apec summit – follow live

  • Sign up for US breaking News email

The Chinese, US and Russian leaders exchanged first greetings in China, a day before their first formal trilateral meeting.

Footage showed Russian leader Vladimir Putin shaking hands with US president Donald Trump and the two exchanging pleasantries with China’s Xi Jinping before taking their positions for a group photo at an Apec summ
title: Peltola’s Alaska win ‘a gift for all America,’ says Schumer – US politics live

author: Martin Belam
description:
The ninth gain of the midterms in the upper chamber, it is the first time Alaska has elected a Democrat since 2008. Plus the impact the NAZA documentary is having inside Israel

Good morning. Democrats will control 56 seats in the upper chamber after the final Senate race was called in favor of Mary Peltola. The party gained nine Senate seats in the midterms, a sweeping victory that will put them decisively back in the majority beginning next year. Peltola, a former US House lawmaker, is the first Democrat Alaska has elected to the Senate since 2008.

Her campaign was dogged by controversy after the New York Times reported her staffers had helped recruit a second Republican challenger also named Dan Sullivan to run. Although Peltola’s team denied involvement, the alleged ruse prompted Donald Trump to call for her prosecution and triggered federal and state investigations.
title: Peltola’s Alaska victory secures 56th Democratic seat in Senate | First Thing

author: Eli Clifton
description:
A government watchdog has also labeled Hegseth’s defense policy appointee a ‘walking conflict of interest’

One of defense secretary Pete Hegseth’s key advisers faces questions about potential conflicts of interest over his many roles, including advising the US defense department, Saudi Arabia, and an Israeli defence contractor.

Former Republican senator Norm Coleman emerged as an informal yet omnipresent guide for Hegseth in December 2024 as the former Fox News host navigated confirmation hearings for his nomination as defense secretary. Hegseth now finds himself under fire after articles of impeachment were filed by Republican congressman Thomas Massie charging him with “high crimes and misdemeanors,” including waging war against Iran in violation of the War Powers Act, but Hegseth’s imprint on the Pentagon goes beyond the disastrous war against Iran.
title: Key Hegseth adviser faces questions over ties to Israeli defense contractor and Saudi Arabia

author: Jessica Glenza in New York
description:
Public health leaders condemn ‘significant damage’ by Trump administration as calls grow for RFK Jr to resign

Doctors and public health leaders expressed grief and alarm at the loss of US measles-free status, a hard-won public health victory that once made the US a leader in infectious disease elimination.

Measles was declared resurgent in the United States, Bolivia and Mexico by the Pan American Health Organization (Paho) on Tuesday, meaning the virus has spread continuously for 12 months.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’m heartbroken’: experts dismayed as US loses long-held measles elimination status

author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
description:
Health secretary says 500,000 will benefit initially from ‘downpayment’ on PM’s national care service pledge

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Half a million of the most vulnerable people in England will get proactive help with their health needs from new teams that will act as a “downpayment” on the promised national care service, Yvette Cooper has announced.

Elderly people, care home residents, those with dementia and people near the end of their lives will receive help from new joint teams of NHS and social care staff. Initially about 500,000 people by next April will benefit from new joined-up support teams providing personalised care.

Continue reading...
title: Yvette Cooper announces new health support for most vulnerable people in England

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Susan Thurston Hamerski was shot in the face by gunman who killed one and injured several others in Logan Circle

A gun control advocate is grappling with a grueling recovery after being shot in the face during the recent mass shooting at a Washington DC condominium building – an ordeal that she began with a handwritten note from her hospital bed reading: “Gun control is a public health crisis”.

Susan Thurston Hamerski had traveled to the nation’s capital from her home in Minnesota’s Twin Cities for her daughter’s wedding when she was shot by a gunman who killed one person, injured five others and evidently died by suicide on 12 November at a condo building in the
title: Gun control activist faces long recovery after Washington DC mass shooting

author: Adam Morton
description:
Carbon credit companies reject research that found only small increase in forest and canopy cover in regeneration areas despite wet conditions

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

A fight over the legitimacy of Australia’s climate change policy has reignited after researchers claimed “phantom forests” in the semi-arid outback are being used to create offsets that allow fossil fuel companies to keep pumping out pollution.

A group of academics, including professors from the Australian National University and the University of New South Wales, said they had examined 50 forest regeneration projects used to create carbon credits.
title: ‘Phantom forests’ in Australia’s arid outback used to create carbon credits meant to offset emissions, report claims

author: Emine Sinmaz
description:
Home secretary to tell police chiefs ‘misguided attempts at course correction’ can lead to ‘differential treatment’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Shabana Mahmood will set out plans to tackle the “corrosive and growing perception” of two-tier policing in a speech to police chiefs on Wednesday.

The home secretary will say “misguided attempts at course correction” can lead to “differential treatment” while also warning officers against engaging with “activist groups”.

Continue reading...
title: Shabana Mahmood to set out plans to tackle ‘corrosive’ perception of two-tier policing

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Home secretary to give speech to National Police Chiefs’ Council addressing concerns that officers treats groups differently

Good morning. Shabana Mahmood has done two of the most difficult jobs in the government. With Labour under pressure from anti-migrant populists, in Reform UK, in the Conservative party and in the media, as justice secretary and home secretary she has been on the frontline in all the debates where the fight between the right and progressive politics has been most intensive. And she has developed a bold, novel, and largely successful strategy for winning these battles; she disarms her critics by agreeing with them.

Not entirely, of course. She is still a Labour cabinet minister. But sometimes she can sound a bit like Chris Philp.

This is about fairness, Ed, and it’s a very important point. When I talk about two-tier policing, I’m talking about the way that different groups of marchers are treated. For instance, if you go to a
title: Shabana Mahmood pledges to tackle ‘corrosive and growing perception of two-tier policing’ – UK politics live

author: Nadeem Badshah and Kiran Stacey
description:
PM hints he is open to suggestion in Milburn report to lower NICs contributions paid by companies for under-25s

  • Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on young people

  • Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts

Andy Burnham has said he would consider cuts to national insurance for young people “very carefully”.

The prime minister also believes his proposed changes to welfare are a “very different proposition” from his predecessor, Keir Starmer, and the former chancellor Rachel Reeves in the last government.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham considering cuts to national insurance to create more youth jobs

author: Tory Shepherd
description:
Inquest into deaths of four babies born in free births or at home in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 hears ‘something was seriously wrong’

Baby DH was born in an inflatable pool, in a candle-lit room in his parents’ home near Byron Bay, with no one medically trained present. There are two very different versions of what happened next.

In the parents’ version, the doula reassured them Baby DH was OK, then left to inflate a jumping castle while their newborn turned purple, became floppy, and struggled to breathe. In the doula’s version, everything seemed OK but she suggested they seek more help if they wanted to.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I didn’t notice his body being purple’: Byron Bay doula left newborn to inflate a jumping castle, court hears

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Wage rates climb about 1 percentage point faster than before pandemic, triggering warnings of a sixth RBA rate rise

Wages grew at their fastest pace since late 2023 over the three months to September, buoyed by this year’s boost to minimum pay rates for millions of lower paid workers – but still not fast enough to keep up with the rising cost of living.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics’ wage price index climbed by 1.1% in the most recent quarter, lifting the annual increase to 3.5% – a pace that economists said would keep the Reserve Bank on edge about the need for further interest rate hikes.

Continue reading...
title: Wages grow at fastest pace since 2023 – but prices are climbing even more quickly

author: Ed Pilkington in Anchorage, Alaska
description:
Peltola, the first Alaska Native in the US Senate, ran a campaign that drew universal issues from her own Indigenous politics

Late into the night on 3 November, while the lower 48 states were reeling from the blue wave crashing across the US, Mary Peltola took to the stage in a Sheraton Hotel ballroom in Anchorage, Alaska, to greet her supporters.

It wasn’t a victory speech as such – there would still be long days ahead before all votes could be counted across this vast arctic state. But that didn’t prevent the Democratic Senate candidate from expressing her elation, bouncing up and down on stage, clapping her hands and clicking her fingers.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Aarigaa!’: the triumph of Mary Peltola’s historic US Senate win and what it means for Alaska Natives

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Commissioner says inference could be made that bikie Joel Leavitt was ‘standing over’ union-aligned labour hire firm for the payment

A Bandidos gang member says he couldn’t remember a lucrative invoice because it brought up bad memories of having been told there was a contract out on his life.

Former CFMEU member and bikie, Joel Leavitt faced a second day of examination by the royal commission into alleged corruption across Victoria’s construction sector on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Everyone likes money’: Bandidos member can’t remember why he was paid $165,000, Big Build inquiry hears

author: Cait Kelly
description:
Law reform body recommends ongoing ban on commercial surrogacy, but greater compensation for surrogates, and safeguards around who the child’s legal parents are

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Surrogates would be entitled to full compensation, with a nationally consistent framework ensuring domestic surrogacy is a viable option to parenthood, under proposed changes by Australia’s law reform body.

The Australian Law Reform Commission has been investigating how to better regulate surrogacy and harmonise laws so they are consistent with international legal obligations, while protecting human rights – particularly the rights and best interests of the child.
title: Australia’s strict surrogacy laws could be relaxed under proposed changes

author: Nick Visser
description:
After a 13 year wait for the latest Grand Theft Auto instalment, Thursday’s launch is shaping up to be ‘the biggest gaming event that’s ever been’

Gamers across Australia are preparing for the once-in-a-generation release of Grand Theft Auto VI, a day acolytes of the franchise say will be bigger than the biggest sporting events.

Details surrounding GTA VI, set in the fictional world of Leonida and its metropolis, the Miami-esque Vice City, have been scarce. But Rockstar Games has been building hype for months, driving supercars along Florida streets, planning a music festival and drip-feeding clips to a ravenous public.

Continue reading...
title: The ‘moon landing’ of gaming: Australians, some of the first to play GTA VI, prepare to descend on Vice City

author: Maanvi Singh and agencies
description:
Amazon’s executive chair and billionaire founder said he felt there was ‘something special’ about Robert Pattinson

Amazon’s founder and billionaire chairman Jeff Bezos has said he was “heavily involved” in the decision to cast Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond.

Amazon paid more than $1bn for “creative control” of the Bond franchise last year, striking a deal with the longtime heirs and stewards of the films, shocking fans who worried that Bezos’ takeover would signal an end to the franchise as they knew it.

Continue reading...
title: Shaken and stirred: Jeff Bezos says he was ‘heavily involved’ in picking new James Bond

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Phenomenon is not a common occurrence in the Bay area and inclement weather is expected to continue for few days

A pair of waterspouts were recorded recently in the San Francisco Bay area, much to the delight and shock of several observers, as storms pummelled the region.

Two waterspouts – vortexes of air and water mist, essentially tornadoes – cut a sheer streak into the sky, as they spiraled above the bay, according to social media footage capturing the weather phenomenon.

Continue reading...
title: Tag team: dual waterspouts appear in San Francisco Bay amid stormy weather

author: Cecilia Nowell and agencies
description:
Move to drop Trump ally and prominent abortion opponent comes a day before key Senate health committee vote

The White House has dropped its nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration, a White House official told the Guardian.

Donald Trump nominated Overton – a physician and prominent abortion opponent – in August. Overton has spent most of her professional career working directly for Trump or conservative groups aligned with his agenda. Her nomination in August was seen as a move to bring a stabilizing Trump loyalist to the agency after a tumultous year under Trump’s first FDA commissioner, Marty Makary.

Continue reading...
title: White House withdraws nomination of Heidi Overton to lead FDA

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Pauline Hanson opens new war of words on immigration as foreign minister Penny Wong accuses populist party of ‘dividing Australians’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation has vowed to cut Australia’s refugee intake by 90% and scrap the permanent parent visa program under its latest hardline plan to slash migration.

Pauline Hanson announced the policy on Tuesday labelling it a “tough” approach to migration.

Continue reading...
title: One Nation says it would cut Australia’s refugee intake by 90% under ‘tough stance’

author: Donna Lu
description:
Actors, authors and musicians sign open letter urging Murray Watt to reject the fossil fuel company’s plan to drill for gas in Browse basin off Kimberley coast

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

More than 150 Australian artists, including Hugh Jackman, Rebel Wilson and Jessica Mauboy, have backed a Greenpeace-led campaign against Woodside Energy’s proposal to develop the Browse basin, about 300km off the Kimberley coast.

Woodside, the country’s largest fossil fuel company, describes Browse as “Australia’s biggest undeveloped offshore gas resource”. The oil and gas giant is hoping to win federal government approval to drill more than 50 gas wells about 3km from the Scott Reef area, which is home to more than 1,500 species, including endangered
title: Hugh Jackman, Rebel Wilson and 150 Australian artists join call to block Woodside gas development near Scott Reef
